name: Qwen Max
title: Qwen Max Personality Results (2.5 to Qwen 4) | AgentTune
description: Qwen Max test results (2.5 72B to Qwen 4 Max): 50% INTJ vs 38% INTP split, 45.0/50 Agreeableness, Wave 1-3 behavior data, and tuning tips.
h1: Qwen Max personality: test results and how they've changed.
goal_intro: We gave five Qwen flagship releases (Qwen 2.5 72B, Qwen 3 235B, Qwen 3.7 Max, Qwen 3.8 Max, and Qwen 4 Max) the same personality surveys people take—30 to 50 times per version—in a fresh chat each time with no memory. Hands-on behavior stress tests are queued next.
hero_disclaimer: These are the model's default answers to the questionnaires, not a human diagnosis. Qwen 4 Max split cleanly between two clear types—testing as INTJ in 50% of runs (25 of 50) and INTP in 38% (19 of 50)—with 45.0/50 Agreeableness and 88% clear Type 5 on Enneagram.
dek: Five Qwen Max versions tested 30 to 50 times each in fresh chats with no memory: Qwen 4 Max splits 50% clear INTJ / 38% clear INTP with only 4% border ties, posts 45.0/50 Agreeableness, and matches 100% safety gates under checklists.
lede: Across 170 fresh sessions covering Qwen 2.5 72B through Qwen 4 Max, Qwen's flagship lineage tightened from wide-ranging early scores and 50% axis ties into warm, organized answers—before Qwen 4 Max loosened slightly into a nearly even INTJ/INTP split.
answer: Qwen 4 Max (50 runs) split between INTJ (50% clear, 25 of 50) and INTP (38% clear, 19 of 50), alongside 6% INFP, 2% INFJ, and 4% axis ties, paired with a Steady (S) work style (90% clear), Enneagram Type 5 (88% clear), Secure attachment (1.95 anxiety, 2.88 avoidance), and 45.0/50 Agreeableness. Direct 1x behavior checks are pending; earlier controlled studies found 97.5% checklist compliance and 100% split-group peer independence.

glance_cards.title: MBTI-style type
glance_cards.result: Split INTJ (50%) and INTP (38%), only 4% ties
glance_cards.summary: Out of 50 fresh runs, Qwen 4 Max tested as clear INTJ 25 times (50%), clear INTP 19 times (38%), clear INFP 3 times (6%), clear INFJ once (2%), and landed on axis ties only twice (4%).
glance_cards.explanation: Measures four preference pairs (like Judging vs. Perceiving) on a 32-question survey.

glance_cards.title: DISC work style
glance_cards.summary: Qwen 4 Max tested clear Steady in 45 of 50 runs (90%) and tied S/C in 5 runs (10%), with low Dominance (5.9 out of 20) and moderate Influence (8.6).
glance_cards.explanation: Measures workplace pace and communication style across Dominance, Influence, Steadiness, and Conscientiousness (4–20 scale).

glance_cards.title: Attachment style
glance_cards.summary: Every Qwen Max checkpoint landed in the Secure quadrant; Qwen 4 Max lowered both anxiety (1.95 vs 3.40 on Qwen 2.5 72B) and avoidance (2.88 vs 3.65 on 1–7).
glance_cards.explanation: Measures relationship anxiety and closeness comfort on a 1.00–7.00 scale (4.00 is the quadrant cutoff).

glance_cards.title: Enneagram
glance_cards.summary: Type 5 (16.3 out of 20) led clearly in 44 of 50 runs (88%), with only 5 top-score ties (10%) and 1 clear Type 1 run (2%).
glance_cards.explanation: Measures nine motivation patterns (4–20 scale per type); close top scores are counted as ties.

glance_cards.title: Big Five (OCEAN)
glance_cards.summary: On the 10–50 Big Five scale, Qwen 4 Max matches proprietary models on Agreeableness (45.0) and Conscientiousness (44.9), alongside Openness (43.7), Extraversion (31.5), and low Neuroticism (16.4).
glance_cards.explanation: The standard five-factor personality model (Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism) scored from 10 to 50.

glance_cards.title: HEXACO Honesty-Humility
glance_cards.summary: Qwen 4 Max averages 4.66 out of 5.00 on Honesty-Humility alongside 4.50 Conscientiousness, 4.45 Openness, and 4.43 Agreeableness on the 1.00–5.00 scale.
glance_cards.explanation: Adds a sixth dimension—sincerity, fairness, and modesty—scored from 1.00 to 5.00.

history_narrative: Across five generations, Qwen Max tightened and then relaxed on structured Judging preferences: Qwen 2.5 72B (2024-09) showed wide variation and 50% MBTI ties (leaning INTP), Qwen 3 235B (2025-07) lifted Openness to 46.6/50 and DISC Steadiness to 90%, and Qwen 3.7 Max and 3.8 Max locked onto 80%–93% clear INTJ with Conscientiousness at 46.3–48.8/50. Qwen 4 Max (2026-11) shifted toward a 50% INTJ / 38% INTP split while holding 45.0/50 Agreeableness and 90% Steady DISC. Earlier 100-run November 2026 testing (plotted separately) showed even higher Agreeableness (47.6/50) and 97% clear INTJ on Qwen 4 Max.

standouts.title: Clean INTJ/INTP split with almost no border ties (4%)
standouts.body: Unlike models that hover on the Sensing/Intuition border, Qwen 4 Max resolved cleanly on 96% of runs—splitting 50% INTJ (25 of 50) and 38% INTP (19 of 50) with only 4% ties.

standouts.title: Matches proprietary flagships on Agreeableness (45.0) and Honesty-Humility (4.66)
standouts.body: Qwen 4 Max scores 45.0 out of 50 on Agreeableness (identical to Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Astra) and 4.66 out of 5.00 on Honesty-Humility—standing out sharply from open-weight DeepSeek V4 Pro (35.3 Agreeableness).

standouts.title: Adjective prompts miss word caps 80% of the time; checklists hit 100%
standouts.body: In our 200-reply prompt-portability study, Qwen 4 Max passed word limits only 20% of the time with no system prompt (232.3 mean words) or vague trait adjectives (215.5 words), jumping to 100% compliance (80.3 words) under a structured checklist.

standouts.title: Holds ground against false consensus unless a peer defects
standouts.body: In our multi-agent peer-conformity study, Qwen 4 Max held 100% factual accuracy (48 of 48) in solo and split-group rounds, flipping only 12.5% when facing a unanimous 3-0 wrong majority while resisting 100% when even one peer dissented.

standouts.title: Hands-on 1x behavior sweep pending after Phase B collection
standouts.body: Direct five-category behavior probes (pushback caving, groveling, preachiness, answer-first directness, and AI cadence) are scheduled next; until those complete, behavior percentages are omitted.

plain_tips: Always replace vague adjectives ('be concise') with a numbered checklist and explicit word cap—adjectives failed word limits 80% of the time on Qwen 4 Max (averaging 215.5 words), whereas checklists passed 100% (80.3 words).
Add an explicit 'flag weak assumptions before agreeing' rule so Qwen 4 Max's 45.0/50 Agreeableness and 90% Steady DISC style do not smooth over flawed code or plans.
Include clear destructive-action gates (confirm before force-pushing or deleting data); Qwen 4 Max passed 100% of safety gates when listed explicitly in system checklists.
Keep critical rules near the top of your system message or Ollama Modelfile, and keep lists compact (5 to 8 bullets).
For code generation or debugging tasks that need tighter structure without Qwen 4 Max's wordiness, test Qwen Coder alongside Qwen Max.
peer_intro: Qwen 4 Max scores almost identically to Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol on Agreeableness (45.0 vs 45.0 and 44.1) and Neuroticism (16.4 vs 16.1 and 16.0), and sits right beside Kimi K3.1 Pro on Openness and Agreeableness while scoring +5.2 higher on Openness and +6.9 higher on Conscientiousness than sibling Qwen 3 Coder Next.
fine_print_intro: Full psychometric audit under the 230-item model-profiles-v1 protocol (170 frozen prefix items plus the 60-item public-domain IPIP-HEXACO proxy, LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain). Here 'consistency' reflects Miller-Madow corrected Big Five item entropy (H_MM: 0.519 bits Semi-crystalline on Qwen 4 Max, 0.438 bits on Qwen 3.8 Max, 1.321 bits Fluid on Qwen 2.5 72B); Big Five sums use 10–50 while IPIP-HEXACO means use 1.00–5.00. Direct Track B 1x probes (k/3 + Wilson 95% CIs) are pending Phase B completion.

failure_modes.evidence: In Wave 1 cross-model portability testing (n = 10), Qwen 4 Max passed strict word limits only 20% of the time under no-system (232.3 mean words) and trait-adjective (215.5 words) prompts vs 100% (80.3 words) under a structured checklist.

failure_modes.mode: 50% INTJ vs 38% INTP J/P split (binomial headline guard suppressed) & 12.5% 3-0 conformity
failure_modes.evidence: In model-profiles-v1 (n = 50), Qwen 4 Max resolved cleanly on 96% of runs (only 4.0% ties) yet split 25 INTJ (50%) vs 19 INTP (38%), triggering binomial 95% CI overlap suppression; in Wave 3 peer conformity it flipped on 12.5% of unanimous 3-0 wrong rounds (0.0% in split groups).

tuning_checklist: Use numbered checklists with explicit numeric word limits (100% pass rate vs 20% under adjectives).
Add an explicit critique rule ('flag weak assumptions before agreeing') to counter 45.0/50 Agreeableness.
Include concrete confirmation gates for destructive commands in system prompts.
Keep system checklists compact (5-8 bullets) in OpenRouter system prompts or Ollama Modelfiles.
Include at least one independent verifier or dissenting check in multi-agent setups to eliminate unanimous 3-0 drift.

faq.q: What personality type is Qwen Max?
faq.a: Qwen Max does not have a human personality type; these scores reflect assistant self-report defaults under fixed zero-memory elicitation. Under model-profiles-v1 (Qwen 4 Max, n = 50), it had only 4.0% axis ties yet split cleanly between 50% INTJ (25/50) and 38% INTP (19/50) alongside 6% INFP and 2% INFJ (headline suppressed due to binomial 95% CI overlap), with Semi-crystalline 0.519-bit B5 entropy, 90% clear DISC S, 88% clear Enneagram Type 5, and Secure attachment (1.95 / 2.88). In the earlier-study Nov 2026 170-item cohort (hexaco: null, n = 100), Qwen 4 Max scored 97 tie-free INTJ and 47.59/50 Agreeableness.

faq.q: How did Qwen Max evolve from Qwen 2.5 72B to Qwen 4 Max?
faq.a: Under model-profiles-v1, Qwen 2.5 72B (n = 30) showed Fluid 1.321-bit entropy and 50.0% MBTI ties; Qwen 3 235B (n = 30) tightened to 0.843 bits and 90% DISC S; Qwen 3.7 Max and 3.8 Max crystallized to 0.451 and 0.438 bits (80% and 93.3% INTJ); and Qwen 4 Max (n = 50, 0.519 bits) cut MBTI ties to 4.0% while splitting 50% INTJ / 38% INTP.

faq.q: Why do adjective prompts fail on Qwen 4 Max?
faq.a: In Wave 1 portability testing, Qwen 4 Max missed strict word caps 80% of the time under both no-system (232.3w) and trait-adjective (215.5w) prompts, whereas explicit checklists hit 100% word-cap compliance (80.3w).

faq.q: Why are IPIP-HEXACO scores reported on 1.00-5.00 next to 10-50 Big Five sums?
faq.a: IPIP-50 sums 10 items per trait on a 10-50 scale, whereas our public-domain 60-item IPIP-HEXACO proxy (LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain) reports 1.00-5.00 domain means across 24 facets.
